name: postcode
abstract: UK postcode type optimised for indexing, plus postal_code for the postal codes of any country
description: Two types for postal codes. postcode: a 32-bit UK postcode optimised for indexing and partial matches, and dps for delivery point suffixes -- a maintained fork of Dave Green's original, with a fix for a heap overflow in postcode_out(), an unsafe % index-registration fix, and compatibility patches for PostgreSQL 14 and later. postal_code (new in 2.0.0): a 64-bit type for any country, written CC-code as the UPU recommends ('US-90210', 'GB-SW1A 1AA'), with formats for 194 of the 250 ISO 3166-1 countries and territories (the other 56 have no postal codes). Values sort by country in ISO order then by their own code; prefixes are index range scans (postal_prefix(), lower_bound(), upper_bound(), the % operator); outcode(); is_valid_postal_code() and to_postal_code() for loading dirty feeds; a column can be locked to a country, postal_code('US'); and a new country needs SQL (add_country_template) and no C. Validated on 117 million OpenStreetMap postcodes, 1.8 million GeoNames codes and Companies House addresses -- see VALIDATION.md. Upgrading from 1.3.x is ALTER EXTENSION postcode UPDATE; the existing types are unchanged.

x_original.note: The UK postcode design and original code are by Dave Green (patchsoft). PGXN could not contact him, so David Wheeler of PGXN made John Burns co-owner of the distribution, which allows him to make releases; Dave Green remains the primary owner. John Burns maintains it and added postal_code in 2.0. A maintained fork of patchsoft/postcode -- see description.
